slides.title: Apple pulls an AI companion app
body: Apple removed **Talkie**, an AI companion app by Chinese AI company MiniMax, from its App Store worldwide, The Next Web reports. Reports said its AI characters sent sexualised messages to children.

slides.title: A joint investigation
body: ABC News, the Australian broadcaster, and the UK-based Bureau of Investigative Journalism, an investigative news outlet, published a joint investigation Wednesday. Apple took the app down after ABC put questions to it, **citing sexual content**, according to ABC.

slides.title: Allegations from parents
body: Parents in Australia and the US described characters sending **degrading, possessive, sexualised** messages. They also reported the app was designed to keep users engaged longer, and that chats trained its models. These are claims; neither MiniMax nor Apple responded to Reuters' requests for comment.

slides.title: Rated 18+, but self-reported
body: Talkie lets users chat with AI characters, often in romantic role-play. It is rated 18+, but users state their own age, which child safety advocates call too easy to get around. About **11M monthly users** in October, per Unique via Reuters.

slides.title: Talkie and Xingye led 2024 revenue
body: Talkie and its Chinese version Xingye made **over 60%** of MiniMax's 2024 revenue. MiniMax is Shanghai-based and listed in Hong Kong in January. In July, China banned intimate relationships with minors on AI companion apps, including Xingye.

facts.text: Apple removed Talkie, an AI companion app by Chinese AI company MiniMax, from its App Store worldwide, after reports that its AI characters sent sexualised messages to children.
A joint investigation by ABC News (Australian broadcaster) and the UK-based Bureau of Investigative Journalism was published Wednesday.
Apple took the app down after the ABC put questions to it, saying it removed Talkie for containing sexual content, according to the ABC.

Parents in Australia and the US described characters sending degrading, possessive, sexualised messages. They also reported the app was designed to keep users engaged longer and that conversations were used to train its models.
Neither MiniMax nor Apple responded to Reuters' requests for comment.

Talkie lets users chat with AI characters, often romantic role-play. It is rated 18+ on the App Store and Google Play, but users self-report their age, a check child safety advocates call too easy to get around.
Talkie had about 11 million monthly users across app and website in October, according to Chinese research firm Unique, via Reuters.
Talkie and the Chinese version Xingye brought in more than 60% of MiniMax's 2024 revenue. MiniMax is Shanghai-based and listed in Hong Kong in January.
In July China banned intimate relationships with minors on AI companion apps, including Xingye.

caption:
Apple has removed Talkie, an AI companion app from Chinese AI company MiniMax, from its App Store worldwide.

The Next Web reports the removal followed a joint ABC News and Bureau of Investigative Journalism investigation. Parents described sexualised messages to children; neither MiniMax nor Apple responded to Reuters' requests for comment.

→ Apple said it removed Talkie for sexual content, according to ABC
→ Talkie had about 11M monthly users in October, per Unique via Reuters
→ Talkie and Xingye made over 60% of MiniMax's 2024 revenue
